issues.description: The manuscript gives conflicting accounts of when the resistance interventions/warnings are administered. The introduction explicitly states that the authors decided to place the warning after collaborative recall, but later they state that the interventions are placed before collaborative recall, while the Procedure section actually places them after collaborative recall and after a second filler task. This contradiction undermines interpretation because timing relative to misinformation exposure is central to the theoretical rationale and expected mechanism.
issues.quote: In the present study we decided to place the warning after the collaborative recall (see the rationale for the research below).

issues.description: This statement directly conflicts with earlier text saying the warning would be after collaborative recall and with the Procedure section, which administers the interventions after collaborative recall. Because warning timing is a design-defining feature, this inconsistency makes the actual design unclear.
issues.quote: What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation).

issues.description: The numbered description of the procedure places the resistance procedures after collaborative recall, contradicting the later claim that they occur before collaborative recall. This makes the temporal ordering of manipulation, misinformation exposure, and test ambiguous.
issues.quote: The procedure will consist of four main phases: (1) presenting the original material, (2) collaborative recall (including misinformation), (3) three procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation (and a control condition), and (4) an individual memory test of the original material.

issues.description: The manuscript inconsistently describes the final individual memory test as open-ended in the Methods, but as using a two-alternative forced-choice format in the Analysis Plan. These are materially different outcome measures with different psychometric properties, scoring rules, and susceptibility to misinformation. This inconsistency prevents evaluation of construct validity and analytic appropriateness.
issues.quote: Immediately after the participants are done with the methods of reducing memory conformity (or the control condition), they will complete the individual memory test of the original material... The test will contain 20 open-ended questions

issues.description: This statement contradicts the Methods section's specification of an open-ended final test. The inconsistency is severe because the entire scoring scheme and comparability to prior MORI studies depend on whether the final test is forced-choice or open-ended.
issues.quote: In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.

issues.description: The analysis plan first proposes item-level coding based on whether the partner actually provided discrepant information during discussion, but then states that all discussed items will be categorized as containing misinformation regardless of what was said. These are incompatible coding rules that can materially change effect estimates and bias the memory conformity measure.
issues.quote: For example, the participant had seen a white mug and their partner had seen a green mug. All the answers provided by the partner during the discussion (green mug, violet mug, yellow mug, blue mug) are misleading the participant and will be classified as misleading. However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen, that is, “white mug” ... the situation will not be classified as misleading.

issues.description: This later statement contradicts the prior item-level definition of misinformation exposure. Treating all discussed items as if they contained misinformation, regardless of actual discussion content, creates misclassification and invalidates the key within-subject manipulation.
issues.quote: In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner’s differing version of events.

issues.description: Participants are tested in pairs, randomized by pair, and mutually influence each other during discussion. Yet the proposed analyses treat observations as if each participant were independent in a standard ANOVA. This violates the independence assumption because responses within dyads are clustered. Ignoring dyadic nesting can bias standard errors and inflate Type I error. The design requires analysis at the dyad-cluster level or mixed-effects modeling with pair as a random effect.
issues.quote: The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs).

issues.description: Because randomization and social exposure occur at the pair level, power analysis based on 240 individual participants rather than 120 dyads likely overstates effective sample size. The manuscript never accounts for intradyad dependence in either power analysis or planned inference.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old... The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs).

issues.description: Although the design section says discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced, the Procedure section says every pair will discuss the same set of four critical details. That means item assignment to discussed vs. non-discussed is not counterbalanced across pairs, creating confounding of discussion status with item content/difficulty.
issues.quote: In the study, the memory conformity effect will be measured in a within-subjects design and discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced.

issues.description: This directly contradicts the earlier claim of full counterbalancing. If all pairs discuss the same four critical items, discussed status is item-confounded, limiting internal validity and making item effects inseparable from misinformation effects.
issues.quote: In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.

issues.description: The three intervention conditions are not matched on procedure, modality, task demands, experimenter contact, and likely duration. Two are podcasts, one includes an active DRM memory task plus individualized feedback plus a motivational podcast. Any group differences could reflect task engagement, fatigue, arousal, self-relevance, or experimenter interaction rather than the intended mechanism. This severely compromises causal attribution among interventions.
issues.quote: First, in order to demonstrate to participants that they are vulnerable to influence, a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used... The results will be fed back to participants... Next, the participants’ motivation to resist memory suggestibility will consist in them listening to a podcast

issues.description: The 'Demonstration and motivation' condition combines at least two active ingredients—false-memory demonstration and moral/motivational instruction—so any effect cannot be attributed to either component. This undermines construct validity of the named intervention and the theoretical comparison with the other conditions.
issues.quote: The third method of reducing suggestive influence in the context of memory conformity is called Demonstration and motivation. In essence, it consists of two elements: (1) directly demonstrating the fallibility of memory to the participants, and (2) motivating them to provide correct answers

issues.subcategory: unsupported process claims without process measures
issues.description: The theoretical account hinges on discrepancy awareness, source monitoring, confidence, consistency assumptions, mindfulness, and motivation, but none of these mediating constructs are directly measured in the proposed design. As a result, any observed group differences cannot support the mechanistic explanations advanced in the introduction and discussion.
issues.quote: Thus, we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies.

issues.description: The manuscript repeatedly argues that intervention effects should depend on participants being aware of discrepancies, yet it provides no measure or coding procedure for discrepancy detection/awareness. Without such a measure, the central moderation hypothesis is untestable.
issues.quote: Thus, we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies.

issues.subcategory: normative influence ruled out without basis
issues.description: The manuscript asserts that normative influence is 'completely ruled out' because the final test is individual. This is conceptually too strong: social pressure can persist internally after discussion through desire for agreement, conformity norms, or avoidance of being wrong relative to a co-witness, even in later private reports. Overstating this exclusion narrows theory inappropriately and may misclassify mechanisms.
issues.quote: Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study

issues.subcategory: potential demand characteristics and hypothesis disclosure
issues.description: The interventions explicitly teach about misinformation, memory fallibility, source confusion, and even explain the deception. This may alter responding through demand characteristics, strategic guessing, or social desirability rather than genuinely reducing conformity. The design includes no control for differential hypothesis awareness across groups and only plans an exploratory post hoc check.
issues.quote: In addition, the podcast will explain why the deception was applied.

issues.subcategory: interventions may alter retrieval/report criterion rather than memory conformity
issues.description: The proposed manipulations may influence response conservatism, willingness to answer, or confidence rather than misinformation acceptance per se. The authors partly acknowledge this by deriving an 'overall number of answers' index, but the design does not clearly distinguish memory change from reporting strategy changes, which complicates causal interpretation of any reduction in misinformation-consistent answers.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers ... (4) the overall number of answers.

issues.description: The planned dependent variables are counts with very small ranges (e.g., number of correct or misinformation-consistent answers out of four or eight critical items). Count/proportion outcomes with bounded distributions violate normality and homoscedasticity assumptions of ANOVA, especially with floor/ceiling effects. Generalized linear mixed models or logistic/binomial analyses at the item level would be more appropriate.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers.

issues.description: The manuscript proposes analyzing four indices plus average accuracy on filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions, and then follow-up pairwise group comparisons, but provides no correction for multiple testing or clear hierarchy of primary outcomes. This analytic flexibility increases false-positive risk.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices... Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions.

issues.description: The manuscript names several possible dependent variables—correct answers, misinformation-consistent answers, other answers, overall number of answers, and average accuracy on several item types—without designating a single primary outcome. This leaves substantial room to emphasize whichever metric yields significance.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices... Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions.

issues.description: The manuscript states that pairs will be randomly divided into four groups but gives no details on allocation generation, concealment, blocking, stratification, or whether assignment is balanced over time. Given pair-based testing and potential experimenter influence, these details are necessary for reproducibility and bias assessment.
issues.quote: The participants will be randomly divided into four groups

issues.description: There is no description of whether experimenters administering the interventions, conducting collaborative recall, coding open-ended responses, or scoring discussion recordings will be blinded to condition. Lack of assessor blinding is particularly problematic for open-ended scoring and coding whether items were misleading.
issues.quote: The discussion will be audio recorded.

issues.description: If the final test is open-ended, the manuscript does not explain how responses will be coded, how ambiguous answers will be handled, how many coders will score them, whether coding will be blinded, or what reliability criteria will be used. These omissions make replication and validity assessment impossible.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers ... (3) other answers

issues.description: The analysis depends critically on whether partners actually provided discrepant information during discussion, but the manuscript does not specify how discussion transcripts/audio will be coded, by whom, with what reliability, or how partial/ambiguous statements will be classified.
issues.quote: The discussion will be audio recorded.

issues.subcategory: active control not matched to interventions
issues.description: The control condition uses a podcast on soft skills related to social attitudes, but no information is provided on whether it is matched in length, complexity, emotional salience, or engagement to the other interventions. An inadequately matched control could create artifactual differences due to attention or fatigue rather than the content of the intervention.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.description: The exact scripts or content of the podcasts, DRM lists, feedback wording, and collaborative recognition questions are not provided. Without these materials or a commitment to share them, the intervention cannot be independently evaluated or replicated.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast...

issues.subcategory: missing exclusion criteria beyond technical problems
issues.description: The exclusion criteria are drastically underspecified. The study involves a perceptual manipulation (polarized viewing) and discussion task, but there are no criteria for visual impairments, language proficiency, failure to comply with glasses instructions, suspicion about dual versions, inattentiveness, or failed discussion exposure. Underspecified exclusions permit post hoc decisions and reduce reproducibility.
issues.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.subcategory: no handling plan for suspicion/deception awareness
issues.description: Participants are asked about the study's real purpose only after testing, and responses are reserved for exploratory analysis. Yet suspicion that partners saw different videos is likely to directly affect susceptibility to misinformation. The manuscript gives no preregistered rule for excluding or modeling suspicious participants, leaving substantial researcher degrees of freedom.
issues.quote: Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis of any relationship between hypothesis awareness and performance.

issues.description: The manuscript gives no strategy for handling missing item responses, incomplete confidence ratings, equipment failure after partial completion, or participant-level missingness. Because outcomes are counts over a small number of items, even limited missingness could distort results.
issues.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.description: Because participants are tested in dyads, dropout or exclusion of one member of a pair has implications for the partner's data and for clustering. The manuscript does not state whether the remaining participant's data would be retained, how partial dyads would be handled, or how such cases affect pair-level randomization.
issues.quote: The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs).

issues.subcategory: questionable effect-size conversion for repeated-measures design
issues.description: The power analysis converts a pooled Hedges' g from prior studies into Cohen's f for repeated-measures ANOVA without adequately justifying the transformation or matching the metric to the intended design. Since repeated-measures effect sizes depend on within-person correlation and variance structure, this conversion may be inaccurate. The use of only two studies with highly heterogeneous effects further weakens the estimate.
issues.quote: The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges’ g = 1.92, N = 55 (Ito et al., 2019) and Hedges’ g = 0.38, N = 74 (Kękuś et al., 2020)... This amounts to a Cohen f of about 0.57.

issues.subcategory: meta-analytic pooling from two heterogeneous studies
issues.description: The manuscript pools only two studies with very discrepant effects (g = 1.92 vs 0.38) to estimate the replication effect size and then bases power on the pooled estimate. With only two studies, a random-effects synthesis is unstable and a pooled estimate of 1.13 is unreliable for planning. This may lead to severe under- or over-powering.
issues.quote: Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13.

issues.subcategory: directional significance tests in ANOVA comparisons
issues.description: The power analysis assumes directional significance tests for pairwise group comparisons in a repeated-measures interaction context, but the manuscript does not justify one-tailed tests or commit to using them in the actual analysis. One-tailed assumptions can artificially reduce required sample size.
issues.quote: Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed.

issues.subcategory: power analysis not aligned with planned item-level structure
issues.description: The power analysis is based on participant-level repeated-measures ANOVA, but the actual data are item-based (multiple critical items nested within participants nested within pairs). Ignoring item-level variance and clustering means the power calculation does not match the proposed data-generating structure.
issues.quote: The option used in G*Power was ‘ANOVA: Repeated measures, within-between’.

issues.subcategory: education intervention may reduce confidence rather than resistance
issues.description: The authors acknowledge that educating participants about memory fallibility could lower confidence and potentially increase suggestibility, but the study lacks a direct measure to distinguish improved source monitoring from reduced confidence. As designed, null or adverse effects would be difficult to interpret in construct-valid terms.
issues.quote: presenting participants with research confirming the fallibility of memory may result in decreased confidence in their own memory, which, in turn, might result in increased suggestibility.

issues.description: Participants will rate certainty from 0% to 100% for each answer, but no analysis plan for confidence is provided despite extensive theoretical discussion of confidence and reliance on one's own memory. This is a missed manipulation/process check and leaves selective analysis possible.
issues.quote: for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% (complete uncertainty, guessing) to 100% (absolute certainty).

issues.description: The manuscript proposes using DRM results as a predictor of MORI outcomes but does not specify the outcome, model, covariates, coding, or whether this analysis is confirmatory or exploratory. This leaves broad flexibility in post hoc modeling.
issues.quote: As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique.

issues.subcategory: possible contamination within pair during intervention phase
issues.description: Interventions appear to be delivered to both members of a pair together after they have discussed the event. The manuscript does not clarify whether partners remain co-present during podcasts/DRM or whether they can continue interacting. Continued interaction could differentially reinforce or alter misinformation and create uncontrolled social influences.
issues.quote: After that, the third phase will take place: it will consist in the procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation that were described above.

issues.description: There are no checks that participants attended to, understood, or were affected by the podcasts, warning, DRM feedback, or motivational content. Without manipulation checks, null effects are uninterpretable and mechanism claims cannot be evaluated.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast...

issues.description: Participants are limited to ages 16–35, likely recruited from media/internet volunteers. This narrow, convenience sample limits generalization to actual eyewitness populations, including older adults who may be especially relevant in legal settings. The manuscript does not sufficiently temper practical claims.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.

issues.description: The manuscript argues that the MORI technique brings laboratory conditions closer to real life and that preparing a witness before misinformation reaches them is realistic, but the task remains an artificial short silent video, immediate discussion, and brief interventions. Strong applied claims to justice systems should be tempered.
issues.quote: The main reason for its popularity is the fact that the MORI technique brings laboratory conditions closer to the real-life situations in which witnesses discuss a crime and are then individually interviewed by law enforcement officers.

issues.description: The manuscript frames the pre-exposure interventions as inoculation against misinformation, but elsewhere says warning is after collaborative recall and also uses mechanisms from post-warning literature. The theoretical integration of pre-warning, post-warning, and inoculation is conceptually muddled, making predictions difficult to falsify.
issues.quote: What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase... The main reason for that is that we wanted to inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take effect.

issues.subcategory: discussion exposure may vary substantially but not controlled
issues.description: Although all pairs discuss four critical items, actual exposure to misinformation likely varies by discussion quality, dominance, agreement, and whether the partner states the discrepant detail. The manuscript does not plan to quantify exposure strength or include discussion characteristics as covariates, despite audio recording discussions.
issues.quote: If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented. The discussion will be audio recorded.

issues.subcategory: outcome conflates exposure with conformity on discussed items
issues.description: The key contrast of discussed vs. non-discussed items assumes discussed items index misinformation exposure and non-discussed items serve as control. But discussed items may differ not only by misinformation exposure but also by retrieval practice, elaboration, attention, and social rehearsal. Without item counterbalancing and direct exposure coding, the contrast is not a pure measure of conformity.
issues.quote: The correctness of answers to questions concerning discussed and non-discussed details will be compared.

issues.description: The manuscript restricts age range to avoid age-mismatch confounds but does not report whether partners are strangers, acquaintances, same-sex, or mixed-sex, despite prior literature showing relationship and credibility effects on memory conformity. These variables may need control or at least documentation.
issues.quote: The age of the participants will be restricted in order to avoid a situation in which a very young participant would discuss the original material with an elderly one, which would possibly activate some confounding factors

issues.subcategory: deception may be compromised by MORI visibility issues
issues.description: Successful MORI procedures depend on participants not noticing different versions or peeking around filters. The manuscript gives instructions but no objective check of whether participants maintained proper viewing or suspected dual projections before discussion. Failure of deception would directly alter the manipulation.
issues.quote: Please make sure you watch the movie through the glasses (no peeking over the top or around the side) and keep your sunglasses on until I ask you to remove them.

issues.description: Although this appears to be a Stage 1/registered report style submission, the manuscript does not specify recruitment stopping rules beyond a target N, whether replacement of excluded participants will occur, or whether data collection could stop early. These omissions matter for transparency.
issues.quote: The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs).
